bug_semantics: ScpClient.Download(string, DirectoryInfo) starts a recursive SCP receive and trusts the filename captured from each server-controlled C (file) or D (directory) protocol record. It joins that unvalidated value to the current local download directory and then creates the directory or opens the file for writing. A malicious, compromised, or MITM server can therefore supply ../ components (and, after the later Path.Combine form, rooted paths) to escape the caller's destination and create or overwrite any path writable by the client process. Exploitation requires the victim to initiate a recursive directory download from the attacker-controlled endpoint.
flaw_origin: Commit d96c93abb2f9409281bfb12d2da8622470a4b3e3 first added ScpClient and its recursive directory-download implementation. In Renci.SshClient/Renci.SshNet/ScpClient.NET.cs it parsed arbitrary remote C/D record names and used them directly in local directory creation and FileInfo construction without requiring a single safe path component. Commit 266dbaefe6c1f2bff2ea00c9ac14a246d37079d9 later changed the string concatenations to Path.Combine but did not introduce the trust-boundary flaw; renames, line-ending changes, and the 2023 partial-class merge likewise only carried the existing mechanism forward.
ai_marker: absent: the BIC commit object names human author and committer olegkap_cp <olegkap@gmail.com>; its message is 'Minor fix to ASCIIEncoding / Add ScpClient to support SCP feature with limited featres supported in silverlight and WindowsPhone environment / Add ScpClient test'; the commit object contains no trailers, including no Co-Authored-By or Generated-with marker, and neither author nor committer identity is a bot.
evidence: The first-party advisory https://github.com/sshnet/SSH.NET/security/advisories/GHSA-q939-rpr3-3284 identifies CVE-2026-48798, affected versions >= 0 and <= 2025.1.0, patched version 2026.0.0, the vulnerable ScpClient.Download(string, DirectoryInfo) flow, and direct fix 600be0de543765995a189b5d7cd4efac5007f3ce.

At the BIC, Renci.SshClient/Renci.SshNet/ScpClient.NET.cs:109-126 launches 'scp -qprf' and dispatches the server stream to InternalDownload. Lines 195-207 accept the D-record ${filename} and concatenate it into Directory.CreateDirectory; lines 223-240 accept the C-record ${filename}, construct a FileInfo from it, and OpenWrite the resulting path. No filename validation or containment check occurs.

git log -L 249,352:src/Renci.SshNet/ScpClient.NET.cs at 066f9982e30112df026dfb43cd41d547aa50b09f traces the function through analyzer edits, the 2017 path change, the 2016 line-ending rewrite, and finally to d96c93abb2f9409281bfb12d2da8622470a4b3e3, where the file is created from /dev/null. Targeted git log -S searches for both original string.Format path sinks also identify d96c93abb2f9409281bfb12d2da8622470a4b3e3 as their addition and 3a2725eae28d8829f81d6c34baaa6839f8ba777f only as the later Renci.SshClient-to-src path rename.

Direct parent-tree verification against 96c512fddb159ef2821342c956111a0fac86a984 found neither Renci.SshClient/Renci.SshNet/ScpClient.NET.cs nor Renci.SshClient/Renci.SshNet/ScpClient.cs, and git grep of that parent found no InternalDownload(FileSystemInfo), currentDirectoryFullName, or recursive 'scp -qprf' mechanism. The BIC adds both ScpClient files, proving immediate-parent absence.

History decomposition excludes false candidates: 57a78fc3a42632c1709b3537a43c982d0e8462dc is a repository-wide line-ending rewrite; 42ff9206d22d90af4083ffe8483276daee289bfe merges the existing ScpClient.NET.cs partial into ScpClient.cs; and 266dbaefe6c1f2bff2ea00c9ac14a246d37079d9 replaces the already-vulnerable string concatenation with the still-unvalidated Path.Combine form. The actual BIC is an ordinary single-parent feature commit, not a reconstructable squash aggregate.

Tag ancestry checks resolve 2016.0.0 to a3a8d42e7c8d4ff3f35513fc69f72fa418c1e5a8 and 2025.1.0 to 6390ede31e0101dad1d09bcb98e6dc9a0741c89a; both contain the BIC and exclude the fix. Tag 2026.0.0 resolves to 7b2fd3dbf2c86a80a7b06cea020aa5f821c9902e and contains both the BIC and 600be0de543765995a189b5d7cd4efac5007f3ce, matching the advisory's patched boundary.

The direct fix 600be0de543765995a189b5d7cd4efac5007f3ce adds EnsureValidLocalName in src/Renci.SshNet/ScpClient.cs and invokes it immediately before both server-derived directory and file names are combined into local paths. It rejects empty names, '.', '..', and platform-invalid filename characters; its added tests cover ../escaped/owned.txt, rooted Unix paths, Windows backslash traversal and drive-qualified paths, and NUL.

git cat-file commit d96c93abb2f9409281bfb12d2da8622470a4b3e3 shows author and committer olegkap_cp <olegkap@gmail.com>, one parent 96c512fddb159ef2821342c956111a0fac86a984, and no trailers or AI/bot marker. The NOT_AI decision is based only on this BIC commit object, not on later commits, PR text, or the fix.
reasoning: The vulnerability begins when d96c93abb2f9409281bfb12d2da8622470a4b3e3 creates recursive SCP download support and treats protocol names controlled by the remote server as trustworthy local path fragments. The client asks the server for a recursive transfer, reads C/D records, and uses their filename captures in filesystem writes; ../ can redirect those writes above the destination. Later maintenance changed syntax and file location but preserved the same missing validation, so neither blame-visible rewrites nor the large partial-class merge qualify as the BIC. The immediate parent contains no ScpClient or equivalent receive-and-write mechanism, while the BIC creates it, satisfying parent absence. The BIC is in every available release tag beginning with 2016.0.0 and in the last affected 2025.1.0 tag; the advisory's direct validating fix is absent from those tags and present in 2026.0.0. Finally, the BIC's commit object has a human author/committer and no AI authorship, co-authorship, generation trailer, or bot identity. Because a real smallest BIC, direct fix, parent absence, and release boundary are all established, the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
